paper.title: PaperToSkill: Turning Research Papers into Portable Agent Skills
paper.field: LLM agents, research-method operationalization, and reusable agent artifacts
paper.paper_type_inference: Artifact/method paper with deterministic artifact evaluation and bounded downstream stress tests

problem.statement: Research papers often describe useful LLM-agent workflows for human reading, but a user must manually translate prose about search policies, memory loops, validation stages, or interface contracts into an executable agent workflow.

motivation.statement: Summaries may preserve an idea while discarding procedural details, validation checks, assumptions, failure branches, required inputs, and transfer guidance needed to apply the method. The paper therefore treats reusable operational knowledge as a distinct artifact from explanation.

claimed_gap.primary_gap: Existing summaries are explanatory rather than operational and omit reusable workflow and failure-handling content.
claimed_gap.positioning_gap: Paper2Agent is presented as the closest concurrent system, but it creates MCP servers from papers plus codebases. PaperToSkill instead targets compact, human-editable natural-language skills with explicit source and failure boundaries, without requiring an MCP server or runnable paper codebase.
claimed_gap.scope_boundary: The claimed contribution is the curated-note-to-skill conversion layer, not robust arbitrary-PDF understanding.

main_claim.narrow_claim: A structured, source-anchored paper-note-to-skill pipeline can produce compact, human-editable, source-grounded skills that preserve more deterministic operational coverage than generic-summary and abstract-only contexts.
main_claim.supported_scope_as_written: Reproducible conversion from curated paper notes to portable skills under deterministic/offline artifact checks.
explicitly_not_claimed: Broad cross-model or live research-task superiority

items: A paper-to-skill schema for operationalizing research contributions
A deterministic extraction scaffold that emits SKILL.md plus source maps
Deterministic extracted-text-to-note scaffolds evaluated on Toolformer and AIDE
A four-paper benchmark over AI Scientist-v2, Reflexion, AIDE, and Toolformer
Deterministic/offline evaluations of structure, context coverage, compactness, source grounding, and transfer readiness
A first single-run eight-row real-reuse stress test that preserves both positive and failed outcomes

method_logical_flow.name: Acquire or construct source-anchored paper material
method_logical_flow.description: The main path starts from a curated source-anchored paper note. An earlier audit-scaffold path can start from newline-numbered extracted text and retain original line anchors.

method_logical_flow.name: Detect and normalize paper regions
method_logical_flow.description: The deterministic extractor normalizes Markdown sections/list items and collects candidates from abstract, methods, experiments, limitations, and transfer sections. The text-to-note scaffold detects broad regions and selects line windows, including a keyword-bearing-column heuristic for two-column extracted text.

method_logical_flow.name: Emit a portable skill package
method_logical_flow.description: The main output is SKILL.md. The schema covers identity, contribution, use conditions, required artifacts, workflow, validation, failures, transfer notes, and source notes.

method_logical_flow.name: Preserve auditability
method_logical_flow.description: The extractor writes references/source_map.json linking generated skill bullets to source-note sections and line spans and distinguishes source-backed content from inferred guidance.

method_logical_flow.name: Apply compactness limits
method_logical_flow.description: Candidate limits constrain artifact size while attempting to preserve method, validation, and failure coverage; the experimental compactness budget is 1200 words.

method_logical_flow.name: Evaluate artifact quality and bounded reuse
method_logical_flow.description: Local deterministic checks evaluate structure, coverage, source grounding, transfer readiness, and compactness; separate saved-response, real-reuse, model-slice, synthetic-integration, and planned external tracks test progressively broader claims.

internal_annotation_track.design: One bounded reviewer, six criteria, 24 paper-by-criterion cells.
internal_annotation_track.reported_summary: 24/24 cells scored; mean 4.75/5; mean confidence 0.946; four discussion-marked rows.
internal_annotation_track.boundary: Internal semantic-fidelity audit, not independent human validation or downstream success.

saved_response_tracks.live_transfer: Four paper packets, each with six saved responses across Codex-style and Claude-style harness prompts and three context variants; deterministic output-contract evaluation.
saved_response_tracks.model_ablation: Two cases across Claude, GPT-family, and DeepSeek slots, with six saved and scored rows and a local output-token proxy.
saved_response_tracks.boundary: Saved-response output-contract evidence, not semantic fidelity, provider billing, or live downstream outcomes.

real_reuse_track.design: Eight locked paper-task rows, one GPT-family run per Summary/PaperToSkill condition, with task-specific metrics and locked local scorers.
real_reuse_track.primary_boundary: Single-run stress test; original-paper references are not locally comparable unless data, input/output, metric, budget, and runtime match.

diagnostic_followups.boundary: Diagnostics and auxiliary sanity checks; none replaces the main eight-row table.

real_reuse_model_ablation.status: GPT-family and DeepSeek-family collected; Claude-family pending after provider HTTP 502.
real_reuse_model_ablation.boundary: Auxiliary model-slice evidence, not a replacement for main rows.

planned_external_track.status: All cells are literal pending external evidence placeholders.

reported_results.result: All four skills score 20/20 on the structural rubric. Skill context coverage is 7.867/9, 8.267/9, 9.1/10, and 8.9/10 for AI Scientist-v2, Reflexion, AIDE, and Toolformer, respectively, above the reported generic-summary and abstract-only scores.

The four skills contain 782, 479, 927, and 943 words, all below 1200. Source support rates are 0.938, 1.0, 1.0, and 1.0 with zero invalid line ranges; the AI Scientist-v2 weak span is retained as a boundary case.
Under o200k_base, skills use 2.39% to 9.65% of the input tokens of full extracted paper text. The manuscript treats this as compression, not billing evidence.
Full skills score 10/10 offline readiness, removal of Transfer Notes yields 7.6/10 for all four papers, and generic summaries score 1.2/10 to 2.25/10.
reported_results.boundary: Supports artifact-readiness signals, not live cross-harness success.

reported_results.result: AIDE-T2 and SWE-T2 favor PaperToSkill; AIDE-T1 and both Reflexion rows are solved by both conditions; SWE-T1 fails for both because patches do not apply; PaperToSkill exceeds Summary on both SNAP rows but all SNAP scores remain below success threshold.
reported_results.boundary: Mixed row-level boundary evidence; no aggregate advantage claim.

reported_results.result: Shared source context makes both SWE-T1 patches apply but not pass; an issue-aligned scorer makes both pass. Controlled and model-generated SNAP executable follow-ups close the artifact contract for both conditions.
reported_results.boundary: These findings diagnose task/scorer/artifact contracts and do not show PaperToSkill advantage.

reported_results.result: Toolformer and AIDE auto-note-derived skills score 20/20 with reported coverage 9.3/10 and 8.467/10, readiness 10/10 and 9.5/10, and source-span support 1.0.
reported_results.boundary: Supports extracted-text audit scaffolds, not robust arbitrary-PDF automation.

reported_results.result: The live-transfer evaluator reports 24/24 scored rows and average normalized score 1.0; the two-case model-ablation evaluator reports 6/6 scored rows and average normalized score 1.0.
The GPT-family slice averages 0.605 for Summary versus 0.333 for PaperToSkill; DeepSeek-family ties at 0.500; Claude-family is pending.

Skill and full-excerpt contexts tie at 0.80 synthetic task success, with mean tokens 86.2 versus 113.2; abstract, generic-summary, and no-context baselines score 0.20, 0.00, and 0.00. Retrieval reaches 1.00 only at K=all.
reported_results.boundary: Synthetic integration and sensitivity evidence, not real-data or broad live-task validation.

conclusion.statement: PaperToSkill converts paper-derived procedural knowledge into portable human-editable skills. The deterministic four-paper benchmark supports compactness, source grounding, structural validity, and greater operational completeness than short summary baselines, while the eight-row real-reuse test is mixed and failure-heavy rather than evidence of aggregate downstream effectiveness.
next_steps: Use human-fidelity annotations as bounded review evidence
Stabilize locked real-reuse rows with pre-registered paired follow-ups
Extend the Paper2Agent artifact comparison to an executable MCP baseline if resources permit
Refine budget, artifact, and failure-recovery contracts using observed reuse failures

limitations_as_stated.statement: The main benchmark converts curated notes rather than arbitrary PDFs; auto-note scaffolds are retained only for Toolformer and AIDE.
Deterministic metrics are partly lexical and can mis-score paraphrases or exact matches.
Saved-response scoring is contract-based rather than semantic or execution-outcome evaluation.
The AI-Scientist-v2 positive result is synthetic.
The 24-cell annotation uses one internal reviewer and is not independent or broad validation.
Cost measurements are local word/token proxies, not provider prices, invoices, or success per dollar.
Real-reuse rows are single-run GPT-family measurements, with non-comparable reported paper references and several runtime/artifact failures.

argument_chain.fact: Paper methods are difficult to operationalize directly.
Summaries omit procedural, validation, failure, and transfer information.

argument_chain.author_claim: Compact editable skills can preserve enough procedural knowledge for reuse.

argument_chain.fact: Convert source-anchored notes into SKILL.md and a source map using a deterministic extraction schema and compactness limits.

argument_chain.author_reported_result: Four generated skills pass structural checks and outperform short contexts on deterministic operational coverage while remaining compact and mostly source-supported.
Eight downstream rows are mixed; follow-ups isolate patch, scorer, budget, and executable-artifact contract failures.

argument_chain.author_claim: The conversion layer is supported as an auditable artifact pipeline, but aggregate downstream effectiveness remains unestablished.

figure_table_map.exclusion_fact: The supporting-table file states that its tables are retained for package/table drift checks and are not included in the main AAAI PDF because of the seven-page non-reference limit.

structure_reader_inferences.statement: The paper's defensible core is an artifact-construction and auditability claim, not a downstream performance claim.
structure_reader_inferences.basis: The abstract, discussion, limitations, and conclusion repeatedly delimit deterministic artifact evidence from mixed downstream outcomes.

structure_reader_inferences.statement: The argument has two nested evidence ladders: deterministic artifact validity is the completed primary ladder, while human semantic fidelity and repeated cross-model real reuse form an incomplete external ladder.
structure_reader_inferences.basis: The first figure caption separates local and external evidence, and both external-evidence tables remain pending.

structure_reader_inferences.statement: The downstream experiments function mainly as failure-boundary discovery: patch applicability, scorer alignment, runtime budgets, and required executable artifacts dominate the discussion more than aggregate win rates.
structure_reader_inferences.basis: The failure-analysis table, four follow-up diagnostics, and Discussion convert row failures into method-contract requirements.

structure_reader_inferences.statement: The current manuscript is an internal draft rather than a submission-ready evidence package.
structure_reader_inferences.basis: README.md explicitly says the two external-evidence tables are pending and the package is not submission-ready until external evidence and the page-limit gate are closed.

structure_reader_inferences.statement: Novelty relative to Paper2Agent is asserted at the artifact/interface layer, but this structure read cannot independently verify novelty against the literature.
structure_reader_inferences.basis: Related Work and the bounded comparison describe a natural-language skill versus MCP-server distinction, while no independent literature search was part of this role.

uncertainties_and_unverified_items: Numeric results are manuscript-reported and were not recomputed from experiment artifacts by the Structure Reader Agent.
The two PDF figures and compiled manuscript PDFs could not be rendered in the available environment; visual details beyond source captions are intentionally omitted.
The manuscript calls the four benchmark inputs real papers, but the curated source notes and extraction provenance were not audited in this structure-reading role.
External cross-model live real-reuse and independent human-evaluation tables contain only pending placeholders.
The claimed novelty and closest-work positioning were not independently verified against external literature.
Original-paper reference scores in the real-reuse table are explicitly not treated as comparable local baselines unless all task contracts match.
